<a id="module-canvas"></a>
## Module: `Canvas`

<a id="canvas-canvasform"></a>
### `CanvasForm`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Canvas.ts:540`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L540)

**Extends:** `VisualForm`

VisualForm is an abstract class that represents a form that can be used to express Pts visually.
For example, [`CanvasForm`](#canvas-canvasform) is an implementation of VisualForm that draws on [`CanvasSpace`](#canvas-canvasspace) which represents a html canvas. Learn more about Space and Form in [this guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Space-0500.html).

#### Constructors

<a id="canvas-canvasform-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

*source [`src/Canvas.ts:615`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L615)*

```ts
new CanvasForm(space: RenderingContext2D | CanvasSpace): CanvasForm
```

Create a new CanvasForm. You may also use [`CanvasSpace.getForm()`](#canvas-canvasspace-get-form) to get the default form.

**Parameters**

- `space` (`RenderingContext2D | CanvasSpace`) — an instance of CanvasSpace, or a rendering context. Passing a context is the renderer extension point: any object implementing the context surface documented in [`SVGContext2D`](#svg-svgcontext2d) (the reference implementation) receives this form's full drawing API — this is how SVG output works, and how custom renderers can be built.

#### Methods

<a id="canvas-canvasform-align-text"></a>
##### `alignText`

*source [`src/Canvas.ts:1544`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L1544)*

```ts
alignText(alignment: CanvasTextAlign = "left", baseline: CanvasTextBaseline = "alphabetic"): CanvasForm
```

Set text alignment and baseline (eg, vertical-align).

**Parameters**

- `alignment` (`CanvasTextAlign`; default `"left"`) — HTML canvas' textAlign option: "left", "right", "center", "start", or "end"
- `baseline` (`CanvasTextBaseline`; default `"alphabetic"`) — HTML canvas' textBaseline option: "top", "hanging", "middle", "alphabetic", "ideographic", "bottom". For convenience, you can also use "center" (same as "middle"), and "baseline" (same as "alphabetic")

<a id="canvas-canvasform-apply-fill-stroke"></a>
##### `applyFillStroke`

*source [`src/Canvas.ts:790`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L790)*

```ts
applyFillStroke(filled: string | boolean = true, stroked: string | boolean = true, strokeWidth: number = 1): CanvasForm
```

A convenient function to apply fill and/or stroke after custom drawings using canvas context (eg, `form.ctx.ellipse(...)`).
You don't need to call this function if you're using Pts' drawing functions like `form.point` or `form.rect`

**Parameters**

- `filled` (`string | boolean`; default `true`) — apply fill when set to `true`
- `stroked` (`string | boolean`; default `true`) — apply stroke when set to `true`
- `strokeWidth` (`number`; default `1`) — optionally set a stroke width

**Example**

```ts
form.ctx.beginPath(); form.ctx.ellipse(...); form.applyFillStroke();
```


Set composite operation (also known as blend mode). You can also call this function without parameters to get back to default 'source-over' mode. See [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/globalCompositeOperation) for the full list of operations you can use.

**Parameters**

- `mode` (`GlobalCompositeOperation`; default `"source-over"`) — a composite operation such as 'lighten', 'multiply', 'overlay', and 'color-burn'.

<a id="canvas-canvasform-dash"></a>
##### `dash`

*source [`src/Canvas.ts:881`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L881)*

```ts
dash(segments: boolean | PtLike = true, offset: number = 0): this
```

Activate dashed stroke and set dash style. You can customize the segments and offset.

**Parameters**

- `segments` (`boolean | PtLike`; default `true`) — Dash segments. Defaults to `true` which corresponds to `[5, 5]`. Pass `false` to deactivate dashes. (See [canvas documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/setLineDash))
- `offset` (`number`; default `0`) — Dash offset. Defaults to 0. (See [canvas documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/lineDashOffset)

**Example**

```ts
form.dash()`, `form.dash([5, 10])`, `form.dash([5, 5], 5)`, `form.dash(false)
```

<a id="canvas-canvasform-ellipse"></a>
##### `ellipse`

*source [`src/Canvas.ts:1136`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L1136)*

```ts
ellipse(pt: PtLike, radius: PtLike, rotation: number = 0, startAngle: number = 0, endAngle: number = Const.two_pi, cc: boolean = false): CanvasForm
```

Draw an ellipse.

**Parameters**

- `pt` (`PtLike`) — center position
- `radius` (`PtLike`) — radius [x, y] of the ellipse
- `rotation` (`number`; default `0`) — rotation of the ellipse in radian. Default is 0.
- `startAngle` (`number`; default `0`) — start angle of the ellipse. Default is 0.
- `endAngle` (`number`; default `Const.two_pi`) — end angle of the ellipse. Default is 2 PI.
- `cc` (`boolean`; default `false`) — an optional boolean value to specify if it should be drawn clockwise (`false`) or counter-clockwise (`true`). Default is clockwise.




<a id="canvas-canvasform-gradient"></a>
##### `gradient`

*source [`src/Canvas.ts:814`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L814)*

```ts
gradient(stops: string[] | number,string[]):  Fn(area1:GroupLike, area2:GroupLike)
```

This function takes an array of gradient colors, and returns a function to define the areas of the gradient fill. See demo code in [CanvasForm.gradient](https://ptsjs.org/demo/?name=canvasform.textBox).

**Parameters**

- `stops` (`string[] | number,string[]`) — an array of gradient stops. This can be an array of colors `["#f00", "#0f0", ...]` for evenly distributed gradient, or an array of [stop, color] like `[[0.1, "#f00"], [0.7, "#0f0"]]`

**Returns:** a function that takes 1 or 2 `Group` as parameters. Use a single `Group` to specify a rectangular area for linear gradient, or use 2 `Groups` to specify 2 `Circles` for radial gradient.

**Example**

```ts
c1 = Circle.fromCenter(...); grad = form.gradient(["#f00", "#00f"]); form.fill( grad( c1, c2 ) ).circle( c1 )
```

<a id="canvas-canvasform-image"></a>
##### `image`

*source [`src/Canvas.ts:1365`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L1365)*

```ts
image(ptOrRect: PtLikeIterable | PtLike, img: Img | CanvasImageSource, orig: PtLikeIterable): CanvasForm
```

Draw an image.

**Parameters**

- `ptOrRect` (`PtLikeIterable | PtLike`) — a target area to place the image. Either a PtLike specifying a position, or a Group or an Iterable<PtLike> with 2 Pt (top-left position, bottom-right position) that specifies a bounding box. Default is (0,0) at top-left.
- `img` (`Img | CanvasImageSource`) — either an [Img](#image-img) instance or an [`CanvasImageSource`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasImageSource) instance (eg the image from `<img>`, `<video>` or `<canvas>`)
- `orig` (`PtLikeIterable`) — optionally a Group or an Iterable<PtLike> with 2 Pt (top-left position, bottom-right position) that specifies a cropping box  in the original target.

##### `paragraphBox`

*source [`src/Canvas.ts:1478`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L1478)*

```ts
paragraphBox(box: PtLikeIterable, txt: string, lineHeight: number = 1.2, verticalAlign: string = "top", crop: boolean = true): this
```

Fit multi-line text in a rectangular box. Note that this will also set canvas context's textBaseline to "top".

**Parameters**

- `verticalAlign` (`string`; default `"top"`) — "top", "middle", or "bottom" to specify vertical alignment inside the box
- `crop` (`boolean`; default `true`) — a boolean to specify whether to crop text when overflowing

<a id="canvas-canvasform-stroke"></a>
##### `stroke`

*overrides `VisualForm.stroke` · source [`src/Canvas.ts:737`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L737)*

```ts
stroke(c: string | boolean | CanvasGradient | CanvasPattern, width: number, linejoin: CanvasLineJoin, linecap: CanvasLineCap): this
```

Set current stroke style. Provide a valid color string or `false` to specify no stroke color.

**Parameters**

- `c` (`string | boolean | CanvasGradient | CanvasPattern`) — stroke color which can be as color, gradient, or pattern. (See [canvas documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/strokeStyle))
- `width` (`number`) — Optional value (can be floating point) to set line width
- `linejoin` (`CanvasLineJoin`) — Optional string to set line joint style. Can be "miter", "bevel", or "round".
- `linecap` (`CanvasLineCap`) — Optional string to set line cap style. Can be "butt", "round", or "square".

**Example**

```ts
form.stroke("#F90")`, `form.stroke("rgba(0,0,0,.5")`, `form.stroke(false)`, `form.stroke("#000", 0.5, 'round', 'square')
```

<a id="canvas-canvasspace"></a>
### `CanvasSpace`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Canvas.ts:24`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L24)

**Extends:** `MultiTouchSpace`

CanvasSpace is an implementation of the abstract class [`Space`](#space-space). It represents a space for HTML Canvas.
Learn more about the concept of Space in [this guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Space-0500.html).

#### Constructors

<a id="canvas-canvasspace-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

*source [`src/Canvas.ts:50`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L50)*

```ts
new CanvasSpace(elem: string | Element, callback: Function): CanvasSpace
```

Create a CanvasSpace which represents a HTML Canvas Space

**Parameters**

- `elem` (`string | Element`) — Specify an element by its "id" attribute as string, or by the element object itself. An element can be an existing `<canvas>`, or a `<div>` container in which a new `<canvas>` will be created. If left empty, a `<div id="pt_container"><canvas id="pt" /></div>` will be added to DOM. Use css to customize its appearance if needed.
- `callback` (`Function`) — an optional callback `function(boundingBox, spaceElement)` to be called when canvas is appended and ready. Alternatively, a "ready" event will also be fired from the `<canvas>` element when it's appended, which can be traced with `spaceInstance.canvas.addEventListener("ready")`

**Example**

```ts
new CanvasSpace( "#myElementID" )
```

#### Methods

<a id="canvas-canvasspace-add"></a>
##### `add`

*inherited from `Space.add` · source [`src/Space.ts:64`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L64)*

```ts
add(p: IPlayer | AnimateCallbackFn): this
```

Add an [`IPlayer`](#types-iplayer) object or a [`AnimateCallbackFn`](#types-animatecallbackfn) callback function to handle events in this Space. An IPlayer is an object with the following callback functions:
- required: `animate: fn( time, ftime, space )`
- optional: `start: fn(bound, space)`
- optional: `resize: fn( size, event )`
- optional: `action: fn( type, x, y, event )`
Subclasses of Space may define other callback functions.

**Parameters**

- `p` (`IPlayer | AnimateCallbackFn`)

<a id="canvas-canvasspace-bind-canvas"></a>
##### `bindCanvas`

*inherited from `MultiTouchSpace.bindCanvas` · source [`src/Space.ts:344`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L344)*

```ts
bindCanvas(evt: string, callback: EventListener, options: any = {}, customTarget: Element): void
```

Bind event listener in canvas element. You can also use [`MultiTouchSpace.bindMouse`](#space-multitouchspace-bind-mouse) or [`MultiTouchSpace.bindTouch`](#space-multitouchspace-bind-touch) to bind mouse or touch events conveniently.

**Parameters**

- `evt` (`string`) — an event string such as "mousedown"
- `callback` (`EventListener`) — callback function for this event
- `options` (`any`; default `{}`) — options for [addEventListener](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EventTarget/addEventListener).
- `customTarget` (`Element`) — If needed, this is an optional parameter to set another event target that's not the canvas element itself. See [Technical Notes guide](/guide/Technical-notes-9000.html) for use cases.

<a id="canvas-canvasspace-bind-mouse"></a>
##### `bindMouse`

*inherited from `MultiTouchSpace.bindMouse` · source [`src/Space.ts:391`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L391)*

```ts
bindMouse(bind: boolean = true, customTarget: Element): this
```

A convenient method to bind (or unbind) all mouse events in canvas element.
All [`IPlayer`](#types-iplayer) objects added to this space that implement an `action` callback property will receive mouse event callbacks.
The types of mouse actions are defined by [`UIPointerActions`](#ui-uipointeractions) constants: "up", "down", "move", "drag", "drop", "over", and "out".

**Parameters**

- `bind` (`boolean`; default `true`) — a boolean value to bind mouse events if set to `true`. If `false`, all mouse events will be unbound. Default is true.
- `customTarget` (`Element`) — If needed, this is an optional parameter to set another event target that's not the canvas element itself. See [Technical Notes guide](/guide/Technical-notes-9000.html) for use cases.

**See also:** [`Space.add`](#space-space-add)

<a id="canvas-canvasspace-bind-touch"></a>
##### `bindTouch`

*inherited from `MultiTouchSpace.bindTouch` · source [`src/Space.ts:431`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L431)*

```ts
bindTouch(bind: boolean = true, passive: boolean = false, customTarget: Element): this
```

A convenient method to bind (or unbind) all touch events in canvas element.
All [`IPlayer`](#types-iplayer) objects added to this space that implement an `action` callback property will receive touch event callbacks.
The types of mouse actions are defined by [`UIPointerActions`](#ui-uipointeractions) constants: "up", "down", "move", "drag", "drop", "over", and "out".

**Parameters**

- `bind` (`boolean`; default `true`) — a boolean value to bind touch events if set to `true`. If `false`, all mouse events will be unbound. Default is true.
- `passive` (`boolean`; default `false`) — a boolean value to set passive mode, ie, it won't block scrolling. Default is false.
- `customTarget` (`Element`) — If needed, this is an optional parameter to set another event target that's not the canvas element itself. See [Technical Notes guide](/guide/Technical-notes-9000.html) for use cases.

**See also:** [`Space.add`](#space-space-add)


<a id="canvas-canvasspace-recorder"></a>
##### `recorder`

*source [`src/Canvas.ts:499`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L499)*

```ts
recorder(downloadOrCallback: boolean |  Fn(blobURL:string), filetype: string = "webm", bitrate: number = 15000000): MediaRecorder
```

Get a [`MediaRecorder`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaRecorder) to record the current CanvasSpace. You can then call its `start()` function to start recording, and `stop()` to either download the video file or handle the blob data in the callback function you provided.

**Parameters**

- `downloadOrCallback` (`boolean |  Fn(blobURL:string)`) — Either `true` to download the video, or provide a callback function to handle the Blob data, when recording is completed.
- `filetype` (`string`; default `"webm"`) — video format. Default is "webm".
- `bitrate` (`number`; default `15000000`) — bitrate per second

**Example**

```ts
let rec = space.recorder(true); rec.start(); setTimeout( () => rec.stop(), 5000); // record 5s of video and download the file
```

<a id="module-color"></a>
## Module: `Color`

<a id="color-color"></a>
### `Color`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Color.ts:11`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Color.ts#L11)

**Extends:** `Pt`

Color is a subclass of Pt. Since a color in a color space is analogous to a point or vector in a space, you can apply all Pt operations to colors too. The Color class provides support for many color spaces like HSL and LAB.

<a id="create-delaunay"></a>
### `Delaunay`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Create.ts:912`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Create.ts#L912)

**Extends:** `Group`

Delaunay is a [`Group`](#pt-group) of Pts that generates Delaunay and Voronoi tessellations.
The triangulation core is adapted from [Delaunator](https://github.com/mapbox/delaunator)
(ISC License, © Mapbox); earlier versions were based on
[Paul Bourke's algorithm](http://paulbourke.net/papers/triangulate/).

*inherited from `Group.$matrixMultiply` · source [`src/Pt.ts:965`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Pt.ts#L965)*

```ts
$matrixMultiply(g: number | GroupLike, transposed: boolean = false, elementwise: boolean = false): Group
```

Apply this group as a matrix and calculate matrix multiplication.

**Parameters**

- `g` (`number | GroupLike`) — a scalar number, an array of numeric arrays, or a Group of K Pts, each with N dimensions (K-rows, N-columns) -- or if transposed is true, then N Pts with K dimensions
- `transposed` (`boolean`; default `false`) — (Only applicable if it's not elementwise multiplication) If true, then a and b's columns should match (ie, each Pt should have the same dimensions). Default is `false`.
- `elementwise` (`boolean`; default `false`) — if true, then the multiplication is done element-wise. Default is `false`.

**Returns:** If not elementwise, this will return a new  Group with M Pt, each with N dimensions (M-rows, N-columns).


Zip a group of Pt. eg, [[1,2],[3,4],[5,6]] => [[1,3,5],[2,4,6]].

**Parameters**

- `defaultValue` (`number | boolean`; default `undefined`) — a default value to fill if index out of bound. If not provided, it will throw an error instead.
- `useLongest` (`boolean`; default `false`) — If true, find the longest list of values in a Pt and use its length for zipping. Default is false, which uses the first item's length for zipping.

**Overload 1**


Calls the specified callback function for all the elements in an array. The return value of
the callback function is the accumulated result, and is provided as an argument in the next
call to the callback function.

**Parameters**

- `callbackfn` (` Fn(previousValue:number, currentValue:number, currentIndex:number, array:this)`) — A function that accepts up to four arguments. The reduce method calls the callbackfn function one time for each element in the array.

**Overload 3**


Calls the specified callback function for all the elements in an array. The return value of
the callback function is the accumulated result, and is provided as an argument in the next
call to the callback function.

<a id="module-dom"></a>
## Module: `Dom`

<a id="dom-domspace"></a>
### `DOMSpace`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Dom.ts:33`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Dom.ts#L33)

**Extends:** `MultiTouchSpace`

DOMSpace hosts a Space in a DOM element. It is the subclassing entry point for building
custom element-based spaces; usually its subclass [`SVGSpace`](#svg-svgspace) should be used instead.
Learn more about spaces in [this guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/space-0500).

When using a Space inside a component framework, create it on mount and call
[`DOMSpace.dispose`](#dom-domspace-dispose) on unmount so listeners and the animation loop are released.
For example, in React:
```
useEffect(() => {
  const space = new SVGSpace(ref.current).setup({ resize: true });
  space.add(...).play();
  return () => { space.dispose(); };
}, []);
```
Dispose is idempotent, and a new Space can be mounted on the same element afterwards
(as happens under React's StrictMode).

#### Constructors

<a id="dom-domspace-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

*source [`src/Dom.ts:53`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Dom.ts#L53)*

```ts
new DOMSpace(elem: string | Element, callback: Function): DOMSpace
```

Create a DOMSpace for HTML DOM elements

**Parameters**

- `elem` (`string | Element`) — Specify an element by its "id" attribute as string, or by the element object itself. Use css to customize its appearance if needed.
- `callback` (`Function`) — an optional callback `function(boundingBox, spaceElement)` to be called when element is appended and ready. Alternatively, a "ready" event will also be fired from the element when it's appended, which can be traced with `spaceInstance.element.addEventListener("ready")`

**Example**

```ts
new DOMSpace( "#myElementID" )
```

#### Methods

<a id="dom-domspace-add"></a>
##### `add`

*inherited from `Space.add` · source [`src/Space.ts:64`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L64)*

```ts
add(p: IPlayer | AnimateCallbackFn): this
```

Add an [`IPlayer`](#types-iplayer) object or a [`AnimateCallbackFn`](#types-animatecallbackfn) callback function to handle events in this Space. An IPlayer is an object with the following callback functions:
- required: `animate: fn( time, ftime, space )`
- optional: `start: fn(bound, space)`
- optional: `resize: fn( size, event )`
- optional: `action: fn( type, x, y, event )`
Subclasses of Space may define other callback functions.

**Parameters**

- `p` (`IPlayer | AnimateCallbackFn`)

<a id="dom-domspace-bind-canvas"></a>
##### `bindCanvas`

*inherited from `MultiTouchSpace.bindCanvas` · source [`src/Space.ts:344`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L344)*

```ts
bindCanvas(evt: string, callback: EventListener, options: any = {}, customTarget: Element): void
```

Bind event listener in canvas element. You can also use [`MultiTouchSpace.bindMouse`](#space-multitouchspace-bind-mouse) or [`MultiTouchSpace.bindTouch`](#space-multitouchspace-bind-touch) to bind mouse or touch events conveniently.

**Parameters**

- `evt` (`string`) — an event string such as "mousedown"
- `callback` (`EventListener`) — callback function for this event
- `options` (`any`; default `{}`) — options for [addEventListener](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EventTarget/addEventListener).
- `customTarget` (`Element`) — If needed, this is an optional parameter to set another event target that's not the canvas element itself. See [Technical Notes guide](/guide/Technical-notes-9000.html) for use cases.

<a id="dom-domspace-bind-mouse"></a>
##### `bindMouse`

*inherited from `MultiTouchSpace.bindMouse` · source [`src/Space.ts:391`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L391)*

```ts
bindMouse(bind: boolean = true, customTarget: Element): this
```

A convenient method to bind (or unbind) all mouse events in canvas element.
All [`IPlayer`](#types-iplayer) objects added to this space that implement an `action` callback property will receive mouse event callbacks.
The types of mouse actions are defined by [`UIPointerActions`](#ui-uipointeractions) constants: "up", "down", "move", "drag", "drop", "over", and "out".

**Parameters**

- `bind` (`boolean`; default `true`) — a boolean value to bind mouse events if set to `true`. If `false`, all mouse events will be unbound. Default is true.
- `customTarget` (`Element`) — If needed, this is an optional parameter to set another event target that's not the canvas element itself. See [Technical Notes guide](/guide/Technical-notes-9000.html) for use cases.

**See also:** [`Space.add`](#space-space-add)

<a id="dom-domspace-bind-touch"></a>
##### `bindTouch`

*inherited from `MultiTouchSpace.bindTouch` · source [`src/Space.ts:431`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L431)*

```ts
bindTouch(bind: boolean = true, passive: boolean = false, customTarget: Element): this
```

A convenient method to bind (or unbind) all touch events in canvas element.
All [`IPlayer`](#types-iplayer) objects added to this space that implement an `action` callback property will receive touch event callbacks.
The types of mouse actions are defined by [`UIPointerActions`](#ui-uipointeractions) constants: "up", "down", "move", "drag", "drop", "over", and "out".

**Parameters**

- `bind` (`boolean`; default `true`) — a boolean value to bind touch events if set to `true`. If `false`, all mouse events will be unbound. Default is true.
- `passive` (`boolean`; default `false`) — a boolean value to set passive mode, ie, it won't block scrolling. Default is false.
- `customTarget` (`Element`) — If needed, this is an optional parameter to set another event target that's not the canvas element itself. See [Technical Notes guide](/guide/Technical-notes-9000.html) for use cases.

**See also:** [`Space.add`](#space-space-add)

```ts
clear(bg: string): this
```

Clear the element's contents, and optionally set a new background color. This overrides Space's `clear` function.

**Parameters**

- `bg` (`string`) — Optionally specify a custom background color in hex or rgba string, or "transparent". If not defined, it will use its `bgcolor` property as background color to clear the canvas.

<a id="dom-domspace-dispose"></a>
##### `dispose`

*source [`src/Dom.ts:313`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Dom.ts#L313)*

```ts
dispose(): this
```

Dispose of browser resources held by this space and remove all players. Call this before
unmounting the DOM, eg in a framework component's unmount/cleanup callback. Dispose is
idempotent, and a new Space can be created on the same element afterwards.

This overrides Space's `resize` function. It's used as a callback function for window's resize event and not usually called directly. You can keep track of resize events with `resize: (bound, evt)` callback in your player objects (See [`Space.add`](#space-space-add) function).

<a id="dom-domspace-setup"></a>
##### `setup`

*source [`src/Dom.ts:139`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Dom.ts#L139)*

```ts
setup(opt: { bgcolor:string, resize:boolean }): this
```

Set up various options for DOMSpace. This is usually set during instantiation, eg `new DOMSpace(...).setup( {opt} )`.

**Parameters**

- `opt` (`{ bgcolor:string, resize:boolean }`) — an object with these optional properties: **bgcolor** is a hex or rgba string to set initial background color of the canvas, or use `false` or "transparent" to set a transparent background; **resize** a boolean to set whether `<canvas>` size should auto resize to match its container's size, which can also be set using `autoSize()`.

**Example**

```ts
space.setup({ bgcolor: "#f00", resize: true })
```


### `HTMLSpace`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Dom.ts:334`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Dom.ts#L334)

#### Constructors

```ts

```

Create a DOMSpace for HTML DOM elements

**Parameters**

- `elem` (`string | Element`) — Specify an element by its "id" attribute as string, or by the element object itself. Use css to customize its appearance if needed.
- `callback` (`Function`) — an optional callback `function(boundingBox, spaceElement)` to be called when element is appended and ready. Alternatively, a "ready" event will also be fired from the element when it's appended, which can be traced with `spaceInstance.element.addEventListener("ready")`


#### Methods

<a id="dom-htmlspace-add"></a>
##### `add`

*inherited from `Space.add` · source [`src/Space.ts:64`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L64)*

```ts
add(p: IPlayer | AnimateCallbackFn): this
```

Add an [`IPlayer`](#types-iplayer) object or a [`AnimateCallbackFn`](#types-animatecallbackfn) callback function to handle events in this Space. An IPlayer is an object with the following callback functions:
- required: `animate: fn( time, ftime, space )`
- optional: `start: fn(bound, space)`
- optional: `resize: fn( size, event )`
- optional: `action: fn( type, x, y, event )`
Subclasses of Space may define other callback functions.

**Parameters**

- `p` (`IPlayer | AnimateCallbackFn`)

<a id="dom-htmlspace-bind-canvas"></a>
##### `bindCanvas`

*inherited from `MultiTouchSpace.bindCanvas` · source [`src/Space.ts:344`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L344)*

```ts
bindCanvas(evt: string, callback: EventListener, options: any = {}, customTarget: Element): void
```

Bind event listener in canvas element. You can also use [`MultiTouchSpace.bindMouse`](#space-multitouchspace-bind-mouse) or [`MultiTouchSpace.bindTouch`](#space-multitouchspace-bind-touch) to bind mouse or touch events conveniently.

**Parameters**

- `evt` (`string`) — an event string such as "mousedown"
- `callback` (`EventListener`) — callback function for this event
- `options` (`any`; default `{}`) — options for [addEventListener](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EventTarget/addEventListener).
- `customTarget` (`Element`) — If needed, this is an optional parameter to set another event target that's not the canvas element itself. See [Technical Notes guide](/guide/Technical-notes-9000.html) for use cases.

```ts
bindKeyboard(bind: boolean = true, customTarget: EventTarget): this
```

<a id="dom-htmlspace-bind-mouse"></a>
##### `bindMouse`

*inherited from `MultiTouchSpace.bindMouse` · source [`src/Space.ts:391`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L391)*

```ts
bindMouse(bind: boolean = true, customTarget: Element): this
```

A convenient method to bind (or unbind) all mouse events in canvas element.
All [`IPlayer`](#types-iplayer) objects added to this space that implement an `action` callback property will receive mouse event callbacks.
The types of mouse actions are defined by [`UIPointerActions`](#ui-uipointeractions) constants: "up", "down", "move", "drag", "drop", "over", and "out".

**Parameters**

- `bind` (`boolean`; default `true`) — a boolean value to bind mouse events if set to `true`. If `false`, all mouse events will be unbound. Default is true.
- `customTarget` (`Element`) — If needed, this is an optional parameter to set another event target that's not the canvas element itself. See [Technical Notes guide](/guide/Technical-notes-9000.html) for use cases.

**See also:** [`Space.add`](#space-space-add)

<a id="dom-htmlspace-bind-touch"></a>
##### `bindTouch`

*inherited from `MultiTouchSpace.bindTouch` · source [`src/Space.ts:431`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L431)*

```ts
bindTouch(bind: boolean = true, passive: boolean = false, customTarget: Element): this
```

A convenient method to bind (or unbind) all touch events in canvas element.
All [`IPlayer`](#types-iplayer) objects added to this space that implement an `action` callback property will receive touch event callbacks.
The types of mouse actions are defined by [`UIPointerActions`](#ui-uipointeractions) constants: "up", "down", "move", "drag", "drop", "over", and "out".

**Parameters**

- `bind` (`boolean`; default `true`) — a boolean value to bind touch events if set to `true`. If `false`, all mouse events will be unbound. Default is true.
- `passive` (`boolean`; default `false`) — a boolean value to set passive mode, ie, it won't block scrolling. Default is false.
- `customTarget` (`Element`) — If needed, this is an optional parameter to set another event target that's not the canvas element itself. See [Technical Notes guide](/guide/Technical-notes-9000.html) for use cases.

**See also:** [`Space.add`](#space-space-add)

## Module: `Form`

<a id="form-font"></a>
### `Font`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Form.ts:262`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Form.ts#L262)

Font class lets you create a specific font style with properties for its size and style. A font instance can be passed as parameter to set a form's font. For example, see [`CanvasForm.font`](#canvas-canvasform-font).

#### Constructors

<a id="form-font-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

*source [`src/Form.ts:278`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Form.ts#L278)*

```ts
new Font(size: number = 12, face: string = "sans-serif", weight: string = "", style: string = "", lineHeight: number = 1.5): Font
```

Create a font style.

**Parameters**

- `size` (`number`; default `12`) — font size. Defaults is 12px.
- `face` (`string`; default `"sans-serif"`) — Optional font-family, use css-like string such as "Helvetica" or "Helvetica, sans-serif". Default is "sans-serif".
- `weight` (`string`; default `""`) — Optional font weight such as "bold". Default is "" (none).
- `style` (`string`; default `""`) — Optional font style such as "italic". Default is "" (none).
- `lineHeight` (`number`; default `1.5`) — Optional line height. Default is 1.5.

**Example**

```ts
new Font(12, "Frutiger, sans-serif", "bold", "underline", 1.5)
```

<a id="form-visualform"></a>
### `VisualForm`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Form.ts:25`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Form.ts#L25)

**Extends:** `Form`

VisualForm is an abstract class that represents a form that can be used to express Pts visually.
For example, [`CanvasForm`](#canvas-canvasform) is an implementation of VisualForm that draws on [`CanvasSpace`](#canvas-canvasspace) which represents a html canvas. Learn more about Space and Form in [this guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Space-0500.html).

<a id="module-image"></a>
## Module: `Image`

<a id="image-img"></a>
### `Img`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Image.ts:25`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Image.ts#L25)

Img provides convenient functions to support image operations on HTML Canvas and [`CanvasSpace`](#canvas-canvasspace). Combine this with other Pts functions to experiment with visual forms that integrate bitmaps and vector graphics.

#### Constructors

<a id="image-img-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

*source [`src/Image.ts:48`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Image.ts#L48)*

```ts
new Img(editable: boolean | ImgOptions = false, space: CanvasSpace, crossOrigin: boolean): Img
```

Create an Img

**Parameters**

- `editable` (`boolean | ImgOptions`; default `false`) — either an [`ImgOptions`](#image-imgoptions) object, or a boolean specifying if you want to manipulate pixels of this image. Default is `false`.
- `space` (`CanvasSpace`) — Set the `CanvasSpace` reference. This is optional but will make sure the image's pixelScale match the canvas and set the context for creating pattern.
- `crossOrigin` (`boolean`) — an optional parameter to enable loading cross-domain images if set to true. The image server's configuration must also be set correctly. For more, see [this documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/CORS_enabled_image).

**Example**

```ts
new Img(true, space)`, `new Img({ editable: true, pixelScale: 2 })
```

<a id="image-img-static-load"></a>

*static · source [`src/Image.ts:73`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Image.ts#L73)*

```ts
static load(src: string, editable: boolean | ImgOptions = false, space: CanvasSpace, ready:  Fn(img:Img)): Promise
```

A static function to load an image, returning a Promise that resolves to the loaded Img.
A load failure rejects the Promise.

**Parameters**

- `src` (`string`) — an url of the image in same domain. Alternatively you can use a base64 string. To load from Blob, use `Img.fromBlob`.
- `editable` (`boolean | ImgOptions`; default `false`) — either an [`ImgOptions`](#image-imgoptions) object, or a boolean specifying if you want to manipulate pixels of this image. Default is `false`.
- `space` (`CanvasSpace`) — Set the `CanvasSpace` reference. This is optional but will make sure the image's pixelScale match the canvas and set the context for creating pattern.
- `ready` (` Fn(img:Img)`) — An optional callback, invoked with the Img when loading succeeds

**Example**

```ts
const img = await Img.load("photo.jpg", true)
```

<a id="linearalgebra-mat-static-add"></a>
##### `add`

*static · source [`src/LinearAlgebra.ts:285`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/LinearAlgebra.ts#L285)*

```ts
static add(a: GroupLike, b: number | GroupLike | number[][]): Group
```

Matrix addition. Matrices should have the same rows and columns.

**Parameters**

- `a` (`GroupLike`) — a group of Pt
- `b` (`number | GroupLike | number[][]`) — a scalar number, an array of numeric arrays, or a group of Pt

**Returns:** a new group with the same rows and columns as a and b

<a id="linearalgebra-mat-static-multiply"></a>
##### `multiply`

*static · source [`src/LinearAlgebra.ts:314`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/LinearAlgebra.ts#L314)*

```ts
static multiply(a: GroupLike, b: number | GroupLike | number[][], transposed: boolean = false, elementwise: boolean = false): Group
```

Matrix multiplication.

**Parameters**

- `a` (`GroupLike`) — a Group of M Pts, each with K dimensions (M-rows, K-columns)
- `b` (`number | GroupLike | number[][]`) — a scalar number, an array of numeric arrays, or a Group of K Pts, each with N dimensions (K-rows, N-columns) -- or if transposed is true, then N Pts with K dimensions
- `transposed` (`boolean`; default `false`) — (Only applicable if it's not elementwise multiplication) If true, then a and b's columns should match (ie, each Pt should have the same dimensions). Default is `false`.
- `elementwise` (`boolean`; default `false`) — if true, then the multiplication is done element-wise. Default is `false`.

**Returns:** If not elementwise, this will return a new group with M Pt, each with N dimensions (M-rows, N-columns).


Zip a group of Pt. For example, `[[1,2],[3,4],[5,6]]` will become `[[1,3,5],[2,4,6]]`.

### `Range`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Num.ts:933`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Num.ts#L933)

Range object keeps track of a Group of n-dimensional Pts to provide its minimum, maximum, and magnitude in each dimension.
It also provides convenient functions such as mapping the Group to another range. This class may be useful for visualizing data in charts.

<a id="op-circle"></a>
### `Circle`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Op.ts:685`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Op.ts#L685)

Circle class provides static functions to create and operate on circles. A circle is usually represented as a Group of 2 Pts, where the first Pt specifies the center, and the second Pt specifies the radius.
You can use the static functions as-is, or apply the [`Group.op`](#pt-group-op) or [`Pt.op`](#pt-pt-op) to enable functional programming.
See [Op guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Op-0400.html) for details.

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Op.ts:1668`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Op.ts#L1668)

Curve class provides static functions to interpolate curves. A curve is usually represented as a Group of 3 or more control points.
You can use the static functions as-is, or apply the [`Group.op`](#pt-group-op) or [`Pt.op`](#pt-pt-op) to enable functional programming.
See [Op guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Op-0400.html) for details.


Create a Bezier curve. In a cubic bezier curve, the first and 4th anchors are end-points, and 2nd and 3rd anchors are control-points.

**Parameters**

- `pts` (`GroupLike`) — a group of anchor Pt
- `steps` (`number`; default `10`) — the number of line segments per curve. Defaults to 10 steps.

**Returns:** a curve as a group of interpolated Pt

### `Polygon`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Op.ts:1053`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Op.ts#L1053)

Polygon class provides static functions to create and operate on polygons. A polygon is usually represented as a Group of 3 or more Pts.
You can use the static functions as-is, or apply the [`Group.op`](#pt-group-op) or [`Pt.op`](#pt-pt-op) to enable functional programming.
See [Op guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Op-0400.html) for details.

<a id="op-triangle"></a>
### `Triangle`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Op.ts:900`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Op.ts#L900)

Triangle class provides static functions to create and operate on trianges. A triange is a polygon represented as a Group of 3 Pts.
You can use the static functions as-is, or apply the [`Group.op`](#pt-group-op) or [`Pt.op`](#pt-pt-op) to enable functional programming.
See [Op guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Op-0400.html) for details.

#### Methods

```ts
static altitude(tri: PtIterable, index: number): Group
```

Get a triangle's altitude, which is a line from a triangle's point to its opposite side, and perpendicular to its opposite side.

**Parameters**

- `tri` (`PtIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<Pt> representing a triangle
- `index` (`number`) — a Pt on the triangle group

**Returns:** a Group that represents the altitude line

<a id="module-physics"></a>
## Module: `Physics`

<a id="physics-body"></a>
### `Body`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Physics.ts:885`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Physics.ts#L885)

**Extends:** `Group`

Body is a subclass of [`Group`](#pt-group) that stores a set of [`Particle`](#physics-particle)s and edge constraints. It is usually added into a [`World`](#physics-world) to create physics simulations.
See [a demo here](https://ptsjs.org/demo/index.html?name=physics.shapes).


Apply this group as a matrix and calculate matrix addition.

**Parameters**

- `g` (`number | GroupLike | number[][]`) — a scalar number, an array of numeric arrays, or a group of Pt

**Returns:** a new Group

<a id="physics-body-dollar-matrix-multiply"></a>
##### `$matrixMultiply`

*inherited from `Group.$matrixMultiply` · source [`src/Pt.ts:965`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Pt.ts#L965)*

```ts
$matrixMultiply(g: number | GroupLike, transposed: boolean = false, elementwise: boolean = false): Group
```

Apply this group as a matrix and calculate matrix multiplication.

**Parameters**

- `g` (`number | GroupLike`) — a scalar number, an array of numeric arrays, or a Group of K Pts, each with N dimensions (K-rows, N-columns) -- or if transposed is true, then N Pts with K dimensions
- `transposed` (`boolean`; default `false`) — (Only applicable if it's not elementwise multiplication) If true, then a and b's columns should match (ie, each Pt should have the same dimensions). Default is `false`.
- `elementwise` (`boolean`; default `false`) — if true, then the multiplication is done element-wise. Default is `false`.

**Returns:** If not elementwise, this will return a new  Group with M Pt, each with N dimensions (M-rows, N-columns).

<a id="physics-body-dollar-zip"></a>
##### `$zip`

*inherited from `Group.$zip` · source [`src/Pt.ts:987`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Pt.ts#L987)*

```ts
$zip(defaultValue: number | boolean = undefined, useLongest: boolean = false): Group
```

Zip a group of Pt. eg, [[1,2],[3,4],[5,6]] => [[1,3,5],[2,4,6]].

**Parameters**

- `defaultValue` (`number | boolean`; default `undefined`) — a default value to fill if index out of bound. If not provided, it will throw an error instead.
- `useLongest` (`boolean`; default `false`) — If true, find the longest list of values in a Pt and use its length for zipping. Default is false, which uses the first item's length for zipping.

<a id="physics-body-solve-edges"></a>
##### `solveEdges`

*source [`src/Physics.ts:1034`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Physics.ts#L1034)*

```ts
solveEdges(dt: number, iterations: number = 1, substeps: number = 1): this
```

Solve all edge constraints for one substep in XPBD form. A link's `stiff` value is a
geometric knob: it is the fraction of the remaining constraint violation resolved per
update, independent of the particles' masses and of the substep/iteration counts
(per Müller et al. 2007, the per-pass fraction is `1-(1-stiff)^(1/passes)`), and
`stiff=1` is a rigid projection. Mapping the fraction to a mass-relative compliance
keeps a heavy body exactly as stiff as a light one at the same value.
This is the solver used internally by [`World.update`](#physics-world-update);
[`Body.processEdges`](#physics-body-process-edges) remains the simpler relaxation for direct use.

**Parameters**

- `dt` (`number`) — substep time in seconds (reserved; the geometric stiffness does not depend on it)
- `iterations` (`number`; default `1`) — solver iterations for this substep. Default is 1.
- `substeps` (`number`; default `1`) — the caller's substeps per update, for pass-count-independent stiffness. Default is 1.

<a id="physics-world"></a>
### `World`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Physics.ts:13`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Physics.ts#L13)

A `World` stores and manages [`Body`](#physics-body) and [`Particle`](#physics-particle) for 2D physics simulation.
It advances with a substepped position-based (XPBD-style) solver and a spatial-hash broad phase.
See a [Particle demo](https://ptsjs.org/demo/index.html?name=physics.particles) and a [Body demo](https://ptsjs.org/demo/index.html?name=physics.shapes) on the demo page.

#### Constructors

<a id="physics-world-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

*source [`src/Physics.ts:46`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Physics.ts#L46)*

```ts
new World(bound: PtIterable, friction: number = 1, gravity: number | PtLike = 0): World
```

Create a `World` for 2D physics simulation.

**Parameters**

- `bound` (`PtIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<Pt> representing a rectangular bounding box
- `friction` (`number`; default `1`) — a value between 0 to 1, where 1 means no friction. Default is 1
- `gravity` (`number | PtLike`; default `0`) — a number of a Pt to define gravitational force. A number is a shorthand to set `new Pt(0, n)`. Default is 0.

<a id="physics-world-integrate"></a>
##### `integrate`

*protected · source [`src/Physics.ts:388`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Physics.ts#L388)*

```ts
integrate(p: Particle, dt: number, prevDt: number): Particle
```

Integrate a particle for one substep: Verlet with the accumulated force plus gravity as
acceleration, and the substep-adjusted friction as drag. Forces are read but not cleared
here — they persist across the substeps of one update and are cleared when it completes.

**Parameters**

- `p` (`Particle`) — particle
- `dt` (`number`) — substep time in seconds
- `prevDt` (`number`) — unused; substeps are equal so no time-correction is needed. Kept for signature compatibility.

## Module: `Play`

<a id="play-sound"></a>
### `Sound`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Play.ts:195`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Play.ts#L195)

Sound class simplifies common tasks like audio inputs and visualizations using a subset of Web Audio API. It can be used with other audio libraries like tone.js, and extended to support additional web audio functions. See [the guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Sound-0800.html) to get started.

#### Constructors

<a id="play-sound-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

*source [`src/Play.ts:248`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Play.ts#L248)*

```ts
new Sound(type: SoundType, ctx: AudioContext): Sound
```

Construct a `Sound` instance. Usually, it's more convenient to use one of the static methods like [`Sound.load`](#play-sound-static-load) or [`Sound.from`](#play-sound-static-from).
By default, all instances share a single `AudioContext` (browsers limit how many can be live at once).

**Parameters**

- `type` (`SoundType`) — a `SoundType` string: "file", "input", or "gen"
- `ctx` (`AudioContext`) — Optionally provide your own AudioContext instead of the shared one

<a id="play-sound-dispose"></a>
##### `dispose`

*source [`src/Play.ts:829`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Play.ts#L829)*

```ts
dispose(): this
```

Stop playing and disconnect all nodes (including analyzer and volume), and release stream, source, and buffer references.
The instance should not be used after calling this. Note that this never closes an `AudioContext`: the shared context lives for the page, and a context you provided is yours to close.

<a id="play-sound-freq-domain"></a>
##### `freqDomain`

*source [`src/Play.ts:696`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Play.ts#L696)*

```ts
freqDomain(): Uint8Array
```

Get the raw frequency-domain data from analyzer as unsigned 8-bit integers. An analyzer must be added before calling this function (See [analyze](#play-sound-analyze) function).

<a id="play-sound-freq-domain-to"></a>
##### `freqDomainTo`

*source [`src/Play.ts:709`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Play.ts#L709)*

```ts
freqDomainTo(size: PtLike, position: PtLike = ..., trim: number[] = ..., out: Group): Group
```

Map the frequency-domain data from analyzer to a range. An analyzer must be added before calling this function (See [analyze](#play-sound-analyze) function).

**Parameters**

- `size` (`PtLike`) — map each data point `[index, value]` to `[width, height]`
- `position` (`PtLike`; default `...`) — Optionally, set a starting `[x, y]` position. Default is `[0, 0]`
- `trim` (`number[]`; default `...`) — Optionally, trim the start and end values by `[startTrim, data.length-endTrim]`
- `out` (`Group`) — Optionally, provide a `Group` (usually one returned by a previous call) whose Pts will be reused instead of allocating new ones — recommended when calling once per frame

**Returns:** a Group containing the mapped values

**Example**

```ts
form.point( s.freqDomainTo( space.size ) )
```

<a id="play-sound-static-input"></a>

```ts
static input(constraint: MediaStreamConstraints): Promise
```

Create a `Sound` by streaming from an input device like microphone. Note that this function returns a Promise which resolves to a Sound instance, and rejects if the input device is unavailable or permission is denied.

**Parameters**

- `constraint` (`MediaStreamConstraints`) — Optional constraints which can be used to select a specific input device. For example, you may use [`enumerateDevices`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/enumerateDevices) to find a specific deviceId;

**Returns:** a `Promise` which resolves to `Sound` instance

**Example**

```ts
Sound.input().then( s => sound = s ).catch( err => ... );
```

<a id="play-tempo-every"></a>
##### `every`

*source [`src/Play.ts:74`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Play.ts#L74)*

```ts
every(beats: number | number[]): ITempoResponses
```

This is a core function that let you specify a rhythm and then define responses by calling the `start` and `progress` functions from the returned object. See [Animation guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Animation-0700.html) for more details.
The `start` function lets you set a callback on every start. It takes a function ([`ITempoStartFn`](#types-itempostartfn)).
The `progress` function lets you set a callback during progress. It takes a function ([`ITempoProgressFn`](#types-itempoprogressfn)). Both functions let you optionally specify a time offset and a custom name.
A positive offset shifts the beat earlier (fires sooner), a negative offset shifts it later.

**Parameters**

- `beats` (`number | number[]`) — a rhythm in beats as a number or an array of numbers

**Returns:** an object with chainable functions

**Example**

```ts
tempo.every(2).start( (count) => ... )`, `tempo.every([2,4,6]).progress( (count, t) => ... )
```

## Module: `Pt`

<a id="pt-bound"></a>
### `Bound`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Pt.ts:1010`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Pt.ts#L1010)

**Extends:** `Group`

**Implements:** `IPt`

Bound is a subclass of [`Group`](#pt-group) that represents a rectangular boundary.
It includes some convenient accessors (eg, bottomRight, center) for bounding box calculations.

#### Constructors

<a id="pt-bound-constructor"></a>


Create a Bound. This is similar to the Group constructor. You can also create a Bound via the static function [`Bound.fromGroup`](#pt-bound-static-from-group), or alternatively via the [Group.toBound](#pt-group-to-bound) function.

- `args` (`Pt[]`) — a list of Pt as parameters

```ts
$matrixAdd(g: number | GroupLike | number[][]): Group
```

Apply this group as a matrix and calculate matrix addition.

- `g` (`number | GroupLike | number[][]`) — a scalar number, an array of numeric arrays, or a group of Pt

**Returns:** a new Group

<a id="pt-bound-dollar-matrix-multiply"></a>
##### `$matrixMultiply`

*inherited from `Group.$matrixMultiply` · source [`src/Pt.ts:965`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Pt.ts#L965)*

```ts
$matrixMultiply(g: number | GroupLike, transposed: boolean = false, elementwise: boolean = false): Group
```

Apply this group as a matrix and calculate matrix multiplication.

**Parameters**

- `g` (`number | GroupLike`) — a scalar number, an array of numeric arrays, or a Group of K Pts, each with N dimensions (K-rows, N-columns) -- or if transposed is true, then N Pts with K dimensions
- `transposed` (`boolean`; default `false`) — (Only applicable if it's not elementwise multiplication) If true, then a and b's columns should match (ie, each Pt should have the same dimensions). Default is `false`.
- `elementwise` (`boolean`; default `false`) — if true, then the multiplication is done element-wise. Default is `false`.

**Returns:** If not elementwise, this will return a new  Group with M Pt, each with N dimensions (M-rows, N-columns).

<a id="pt-bound-dollar-zip"></a>
##### `$zip`

*inherited from `Group.$zip` · source [`src/Pt.ts:987`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Pt.ts#L987)*

```ts
$zip(defaultValue: number | boolean = undefined, useLongest: boolean = false): Group
```

Zip a group of Pt. eg, [[1,2],[3,4],[5,6]] => [[1,3,5],[2,4,6]].

**Parameters**

- `defaultValue` (`number | boolean`; default `undefined`) — a default value to fill if index out of bound. If not provided, it will throw an error instead.
- `useLongest` (`boolean`; default `false`) — If true, find the longest list of values in a Pt and use its length for zipping. Default is false, which uses the first item's length for zipping.

<a id="pt-group"></a>
### `Group`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Pt.ts:559`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Pt.ts#L559)

**Extends:** `Array`

A Group is a subclass of standard javascript [`Array`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array). It should only contain Pt instances. You can think of it as an array of Float32Arrays.
See [Group guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Group-0300.html) for details.


Apply this group as a matrix and calculate matrix multiplication.

<a id="pt-pt"></a>
### `Pt`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Pt.ts:12`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Pt.ts#L12)

**Extends:** `Float32Array`

**Implements:** `IPt`, `Iterable`

Pt is a subclass of standard [`Float32Array`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Float32Array) with additional properties and functions to support vector and geometric calculations.
See [Pt guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Pt-0200.html) for details.

#### Constructors

<a id="pt-pt-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

*source [`src/Pt.ts:21`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Pt.ts#L21)*

```ts
new Pt(args: (number | number[] | IPt | Float32Array)[]): Pt
```

Create a Pt. If no parameter is provided, this will instantiate a Pt with 2 dimensions [0, 0].
Note that `new Pt(3)` will only instantiate Pt with length of 3 (ie, same as `new Float32Array(3)` ). If you need a Pt with 1 dimension of value 3, use `new Pt([3])`.

**Parameters**

- `args` (`(number | number[] | IPt | Float32Array)[]`) — a list of numeric parameters, an array of numbers, or an object with {x,y,z,w} properties

**Example**

```ts
new Pt()`, `new Pt(1,2,3,4,5)`, `new Pt([1,2])`, `new Pt({x:0, y:1})`, `new Pt(pt)
```

## Module: `Space`

<a id="space-multitouchspace"></a>
### `MultiTouchSpace`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Space.ts:299`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L299)

**Extends:** `Space`

MultiTouchSpace is an abstract class that extends [`Space`](#space-space) to support user interactions via touch events.
It's extended through subclasses such as [`CanvasSpace`](#canvas-canvasspace) and [`SVGSpace`](#svg-svgspace).

#### Methods

<a id="space-multitouchspace-add"></a>
##### `add`

*inherited from `Space.add` · source [`src/Space.ts:64`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L64)*

```ts
add(p: IPlayer | AnimateCallbackFn): this
```

Add an [`IPlayer`](#types-iplayer) object or a [`AnimateCallbackFn`](#types-animatecallbackfn) callback function to handle events in this Space. An IPlayer is an object with the following callback functions:
- required: `animate: fn( time, ftime, space )`
- optional: `start: fn(bound, space)`
- optional: `resize: fn( size, event )`
- optional: `action: fn( type, x, y, event )`
Subclasses of Space may define other callback functions.

**Parameters**

- `p` (`IPlayer | AnimateCallbackFn`)

<a id="space-multitouchspace-bind-canvas"></a>
##### `bindCanvas`

*source [`src/Space.ts:344`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L344)*

```ts
bindCanvas(evt: string, callback: EventListener, options: any = {}, customTarget: Element): void
```

Bind event listener in canvas element. You can also use [`MultiTouchSpace.bindMouse`](#space-multitouchspace-bind-mouse) or [`MultiTouchSpace.bindTouch`](#space-multitouchspace-bind-touch) to bind mouse or touch events conveniently.

**Parameters**

- `evt` (`string`) — an event string such as "mousedown"
- `callback` (`EventListener`) — callback function for this event
- `options` (`any`; default `{}`) — options for [addEventListener](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EventTarget/addEventListener).
- `customTarget` (`Element`) — If needed, this is an optional parameter to set another event target that's not the canvas element itself. See [Technical Notes guide](/guide/Technical-notes-9000.html) for use cases.

##### `bindKeyboard`

*source [`src/Space.ts:480`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L480)*

```ts
bindKeyboard(bind: boolean = true, customTarget: EventTarget): this
```

Bind or unbind keyboard events. Events are attached to `document` by
default, or to `customTarget` when one is provided.

**Parameters**

- `bind` (`boolean`; default `true`)
- `customTarget` (`EventTarget`)

<a id="space-multitouchspace-bind-mouse"></a>
##### `bindMouse`

*source [`src/Space.ts:391`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L391)*

```ts
bindMouse(bind: boolean = true, customTarget: Element): this
```

A convenient method to bind (or unbind) all mouse events in canvas element.
All [`IPlayer`](#types-iplayer) objects added to this space that implement an `action` callback property will receive mouse event callbacks.
The types of mouse actions are defined by [`UIPointerActions`](#ui-uipointeractions) constants: "up", "down", "move", "drag", "drop", "over", and "out".

**Parameters**

- `bind` (`boolean`; default `true`) — a boolean value to bind mouse events if set to `true`. If `false`, all mouse events will be unbound. Default is true.
- `customTarget` (`Element`) — If needed, this is an optional parameter to set another event target that's not the canvas element itself. See [Technical Notes guide](/guide/Technical-notes-9000.html) for use cases.

**See also:** [`Space.add`](#space-space-add)

<a id="space-multitouchspace-bind-touch"></a>
##### `bindTouch`

*source [`src/Space.ts:431`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L431)*

```ts
bindTouch(bind: boolean = true, passive: boolean = false, customTarget: Element): this
```

A convenient method to bind (or unbind) all touch events in canvas element.
All [`IPlayer`](#types-iplayer) objects added to this space that implement an `action` callback property will receive touch event callbacks.
The types of mouse actions are defined by [`UIPointerActions`](#ui-uipointeractions) constants: "up", "down", "move", "drag", "drop", "over", and "out".

**Parameters**

- `bind` (`boolean`; default `true`) — a boolean value to bind touch events if set to `true`. If `false`, all mouse events will be unbound. Default is true.
- `passive` (`boolean`; default `false`) — a boolean value to set passive mode, ie, it won't block scrolling. Default is false.
- `customTarget` (`Element`) — If needed, this is an optional parameter to set another event target that's not the canvas element itself. See [Technical Notes guide](/guide/Technical-notes-9000.html) for use cases.

**See also:** [`Space.add`](#space-space-add)


A convenient method to convert the touch points in a touch event to an array of Pts.

**Parameters**

- `evt` (`TouchEvent`) — a touch event which contains touches, changedTouches, and targetTouches list
- `which` (`TouchPointsKey`; default `"touches"`) — a string to select a touches list: "touches", "changedTouches", or "targetTouches". Default is "touches"

**Returns:** an array of Pt, whose origin position (0,0) is offset to the top-left of this space

### `Space`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Space.ts:18`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L18)

<a id="module-svg"></a>
## Module: `Svg`

<a id="svg-svgcontext2d"></a>
### `SVGContext2D`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Svg.ts:147`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Svg.ts#L147)

**`SVGContext2D`** implements the subset of `CanvasRenderingContext2D` that
[`CanvasForm`](#canvas-canvasform) draws through, and renders it as SVG. Consecutive shapes that share
paint state are merged into single `<path>` elements ("style runs"), so the DOM cost per
frame is proportional to the number of style changes, not the number of shapes. This is
what lets the same sketch run unchanged on canvas and SVG.

Capability notes: blend-mode composites map to `mix-blend-mode`; Porter-Duff composites,
`clip`, and `putImageData` warn once and no-op. Text metrics come from a hidden canvas, so
`textBox` layout matches canvas exactly. When shapes with both fill and stroke are merged,
all fills in a run paint before its strokes — visible only for overlapping same-styled
shapes.

**Writing your own renderer**: this class is the reference implementation of the rendering
contract — any object implementing the same context surface can be handed to
[`CanvasForm`](#canvas-canvasform)'s constructor to become a Pts renderer (a PDF writer, a command
recorder, a test snapshotter, and so on). The surface is the subset of
`CanvasRenderingContext2D` that `CanvasForm` draws through:
- path verbs: `beginPath`, `moveTo`, `lineTo`, `quadraticCurveTo`, `bezierCurveTo`,
  `rect`, `arc`, `ellipse`, `closePath`
- paint: `fill`, `stroke`, `fillRect`, `clearRect`
- state: `save`, `restore`, `clip`, `scale`
- style fields: `fillStyle`, `strokeStyle`, `lineWidth`, `lineJoin`, `lineCap`,
  `globalAlpha`, `globalCompositeOperation`, `setLineDash`, `lineDashOffset`
- text: `font`, `textAlign`, `textBaseline`, `fillText`, `measureText`
- images: `drawImage`, `putImageData`
- gradients: `createLinearGradient`, `createRadialGradient`

A renderer driven by a Space should also expose a frame lifecycle like
[`SVGContext2D.beginFrame`](#svg-svgcontext2d-begin-frame) / [`SVGContext2D.commitFrame`](#svg-svgcontext2d-commit-frame), called around the
players' animate callbacks. The unit test "implements every context member that CanvasForm
uses" is the compatibility alarm: it fails when a new `CanvasForm` feature touches a
context member a renderer does not implement.

<a id="svg-svgform"></a>
### `SVGForm`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Svg.ts:922`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Svg.ts#L922)

**Extends:** `CanvasForm`

SVGForm is a [`CanvasForm`](#canvas-canvasform) rendered through a [`SVGContext2D`](#svg-svgcontext2d): it inherits
the complete canvas drawing API — shapes, gradients, dashes, images, `textBox` — with SVG
output, so a sketch can swap between `CanvasSpace` and `SVGSpace` without changing any
drawing code. The legacy per-element static helpers and `scope()` workflow are retained
for compatibility but are no longer needed.

<a id="svg-svgform-align-text"></a>
##### `alignText`

*inherited from `CanvasForm.alignText` · source [`src/Canvas.ts:1544`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L1544)*

```ts
alignText(alignment: CanvasTextAlign = "left", baseline: CanvasTextBaseline = "alphabetic"): SVGForm
```

Set text alignment and baseline (eg, vertical-align).

**Parameters**

- `alignment` (`CanvasTextAlign`; default `"left"`) — HTML canvas' textAlign option: "left", "right", "center", "start", or "end"
- `baseline` (`CanvasTextBaseline`; default `"alphabetic"`) — HTML canvas' textBaseline option: "top", "hanging", "middle", "alphabetic", "ideographic", "bottom". For convenience, you can also use "center" (same as "middle"), and "baseline" (same as "alphabetic")

<a id="svg-svgform-apply-fill-stroke"></a>
##### `applyFillStroke`

*inherited from `CanvasForm.applyFillStroke` · source [`src/Canvas.ts:790`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L790)*

```ts
applyFillStroke(filled: string | boolean = true, stroked: string | boolean = true, strokeWidth: number = 1): SVGForm
```

A convenient function to apply fill and/or stroke after custom drawings using canvas context (eg, `form.ctx.ellipse(...)`).
You don't need to call this function if you're using Pts' drawing functions like `form.point` or `form.rect`

**Parameters**

- `filled` (`string | boolean`; default `true`) — apply fill when set to `true`
- `stroked` (`string | boolean`; default `true`) — apply stroke when set to `true`
- `strokeWidth` (`number`; default `1`) — optionally set a stroke width

**Example**

```ts
form.ctx.beginPath(); form.ctx.ellipse(...); form.applyFillStroke();
```

<a id="svg-svgform-dash"></a>
##### `dash`

*inherited from `CanvasForm.dash` · source [`src/Canvas.ts:881`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L881)*

```ts
dash(segments: boolean | PtLike = true, offset: number = 0): this
```

Activate dashed stroke and set dash style. You can customize the segments and offset.

**Parameters**

- `segments` (`boolean | PtLike`; default `true`) — Dash segments. Defaults to `true` which corresponds to `[5, 5]`. Pass `false` to deactivate dashes. (See [canvas documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/setLineDash))
- `offset` (`number`; default `0`) — Dash offset. Defaults to 0. (See [canvas documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/lineDashOffset)

**Example**

```ts
form.dash()`, `form.dash([5, 10])`, `form.dash([5, 5], 5)`, `form.dash(false)
```

<a id="svg-svgform-gradient"></a>
##### `gradient`

*inherited from `CanvasForm.gradient` · source [`src/Canvas.ts:814`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L814)*

```ts
gradient(stops: string[] | number,string[]):  Fn(area1:GroupLike, area2:GroupLike)
```

This function takes an array of gradient colors, and returns a function to define the areas of the gradient fill. See demo code in [CanvasForm.gradient](https://ptsjs.org/demo/?name=canvasform.textBox).

**Parameters**

- `stops` (`string[] | number,string[]`) — an array of gradient stops. This can be an array of colors `["#f00", "#0f0", ...]` for evenly distributed gradient, or an array of [stop, color] like `[[0.1, "#f00"], [0.7, "#0f0"]]`

**Returns:** a function that takes 1 or 2 `Group` as parameters. Use a single `Group` to specify a rectangular area for linear gradient, or use 2 `Groups` to specify 2 `Circles` for radial gradient.

**Example**

```ts
c1 = Circle.fromCenter(...); grad = form.gradient(["#f00", "#00f"]); form.fill( grad( c1, c2 ) ).circle( c1 )
```

<a id="svg-svgspace"></a>
### `SVGSpace`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Svg.ts:692`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Svg.ts#L692)

**Extends:** `DOMSpace`

SVGSpace extends [`DOMSpace`](#dom-domspace) to support SVG elements. Use it with [`SVGForm`](#svg-svgform),
which shares its drawing API and semantics with [`CanvasForm`](#canvas-canvasform) — a sketch written for
canvas runs on SVG unchanged. Check out the [Space guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Space-0500.html) for details.

#### Constructors

<a id="svg-svgspace-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

*overrides `DOMSpace.__constructor` · source [`src/Svg.ts:704`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Svg.ts#L704)*

```ts
new SVGSpace(elem: string | Element, callback: Function): SVGSpace
```

Create a SVGSpace which represents a Space for SVG elements.

**Parameters**

- `elem` (`string | Element`) — Specify an element by its "id" attribute as string, or by the element object itself. An element can be an existing `<svg>`, or a `<div>` container in which a new `<svg>` will be created. If left empty, a `<div id="pt_container"><svg id="pt" /></div>` will be added to DOM. Use css to customize its appearance if needed.
- `callback` (`Function`) — an optional callback `function(boundingBox, spaceElement)` to be called when canvas is appended and ready. Alternatively, a "ready" event will also be fired from the `<svg>` element when it's appended, which can be traced with `spaceInstance.canvas.addEventListener("ready")`

**Example**

```ts
new SVGSpace( "#myElementID" )
```

#### Methods

<a id="svg-svgspace-add"></a>
##### `add`

*inherited from `Space.add` · source [`src/Space.ts:64`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L64)*

```ts
add(p: IPlayer | AnimateCallbackFn): this
```

Add an [`IPlayer`](#types-iplayer) object or a [`AnimateCallbackFn`](#types-animatecallbackfn) callback function to handle events in this Space. An IPlayer is an object with the following callback functions:
- required: `animate: fn( time, ftime, space )`
- optional: `start: fn(bound, space)`
- optional: `resize: fn( size, event )`
- optional: `action: fn( type, x, y, event )`
Subclasses of Space may define other callback functions.

**Parameters**

- `p` (`IPlayer | AnimateCallbackFn`)

<a id="svg-svgspace-bind-canvas"></a>
##### `bindCanvas`

*inherited from `MultiTouchSpace.bindCanvas` · source [`src/Space.ts:344`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L344)*

```ts
bindCanvas(evt: string, callback: EventListener, options: any = {}, customTarget: Element): void
```

Bind event listener in canvas element. You can also use [`MultiTouchSpace.bindMouse`](#space-multitouchspace-bind-mouse) or [`MultiTouchSpace.bindTouch`](#space-multitouchspace-bind-touch) to bind mouse or touch events conveniently.

**Parameters**

- `evt` (`string`) — an event string such as "mousedown"
- `callback` (`EventListener`) — callback function for this event
- `options` (`any`; default `{}`) — options for [addEventListener](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EventTarget/addEventListener).
- `customTarget` (`Element`) — If needed, this is an optional parameter to set another event target that's not the canvas element itself. See [Technical Notes guide](/guide/Technical-notes-9000.html) for use cases.

```ts
bindKeyboard(bind: boolean = true, customTarget: EventTarget): this
```

Bind or unbind keyboard events. Events are attached to `document` by
default, or to `customTarget` when one is provided.

**Parameters**

- `bind` (`boolean`; default `true`)
- `customTarget` (`EventTarget`)

<a id="svg-svgspace-bind-mouse"></a>
##### `bindMouse`

*inherited from `MultiTouchSpace.bindMouse` · source [`src/Space.ts:391`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L391)*

```ts
bindMouse(bind: boolean = true, customTarget: Element): this
```

A convenient method to bind (or unbind) all mouse events in canvas element.
All [`IPlayer`](#types-iplayer) objects added to this space that implement an `action` callback property will receive mouse event callbacks.
The types of mouse actions are defined by [`UIPointerActions`](#ui-uipointeractions) constants: "up", "down", "move", "drag", "drop", "over", and "out".

**Parameters**

- `bind` (`boolean`; default `true`) — a boolean value to bind mouse events if set to `true`. If `false`, all mouse events will be unbound. Default is true.
- `customTarget` (`Element`) — If needed, this is an optional parameter to set another event target that's not the canvas element itself. See [Technical Notes guide](/guide/Technical-notes-9000.html) for use cases.

**See also:** [`Space.add`](#space-space-add)

<a id="svg-svgspace-bind-touch"></a>
##### `bindTouch`

*inherited from `MultiTouchSpace.bindTouch` · source [`src/Space.ts:431`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Space.ts#L431)*

```ts
bindTouch(bind: boolean = true, passive: boolean = false, customTarget: Element): this
```

A convenient method to bind (or unbind) all touch events in canvas element.
All [`IPlayer`](#types-iplayer) objects added to this space that implement an `action` callback property will receive touch event callbacks.
The types of mouse actions are defined by [`UIPointerActions`](#ui-uipointeractions) constants: "up", "down", "move", "drag", "drop", "over", and "out".

**Parameters**

- `bind` (`boolean`; default `true`) — a boolean value to bind touch events if set to `true`. If `false`, all mouse events will be unbound. Default is true.
- `passive` (`boolean`; default `false`) — a boolean value to set passive mode, ie, it won't block scrolling. Default is false.
- `customTarget` (`Element`) — If needed, this is an optional parameter to set another event target that's not the canvas element itself. See [Technical Notes guide](/guide/Technical-notes-9000.html) for use cases.

**See also:** [`Space.add`](#space-space-add)

<a id="module-typography"></a>
## Module: `Typography`

<a id="typography-typography"></a>
### `Typography`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Typography.ts:10`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Typography.ts#L10)

Typography provides helper functions to support typographic layouts. For a concrete example, see [a demo here](https://ptsjs.org/demo/index.html?name=canvasform.textBox) that uses the [`CanvasForm.textBox`](#canvas-canvasform-text-box) function.

#### Methods

<a id="typography-typography-static-font-size-to-box"></a>
##### `fontSizeToBox`

*static · source [`src/Typography.ts:56`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Typography.ts#L56)*

```ts
static fontSizeToBox(box: PtLikeIterable, ratio: number = 1, byHeight: boolean = true):  Fn(GroupLike:any)
```

Get a function to scale font size proportionally to text box size changes.

**Parameters**

- `box` (`PtLikeIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<PtLike> representing the initial box
- `ratio` (`number`; default `1`) — font-size change ratio. Default is 1.
- `byHeight` (`boolean`; default `true`)

**Returns:** a function where input parameter is a new box, and returns the new font size value

<a id="typography-typography-static-font-size-to-threshold"></a>
##### `fontSizeToThreshold`

*static · source [`src/Typography.ts:78`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Typography.ts#L78)*

```ts
static fontSizeToThreshold(threshold: number, direction: number = 0):  Fn(a:number, b:number)
```

Get a function to scale font size based on a threshold value.

**Parameters**

- `threshold` (`number`) — threshold value
- `direction` (`number`; default `0`) — if negative, get a font size <= defaultSize; if positive, get a font size >= defaultSize; Default is 0 which will scale font without min or max limits.

**Returns:** a function where input parameter is the default font size and a value to compare with threshold, and returns new font size value

<a id="typography-typography-static-text-width-estimator"></a>
##### `textWidthEstimator`

*static · source [`src/Typography.ts:18`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Typography.ts#L18)*

```ts
static textWidthEstimator(fn:  Fn(string:any), samples: string[] = ..., distribution: number[] = ...):  Fn(string:any)
```

Create a heuristic text width estimate function. It will be less accurate but faster.

**Parameters**

- `fn` (` Fn(string:any)`) — a reference function that can measure text width accurately
- `samples` (`string[]`; default `...`) — a list of string samples. Default is ["M", "n", "."]
- `distribution` (`number[]`; default `...`) — a list of the samples' probability distribution. Default is [0.06, 0.8, 0.14].

**Returns:** a function that can estimate text width

<a id="typography-typography-static-truncate"></a>
##### `truncate`

*static · source [`src/Typography.ts:35`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Typography.ts#L35)*

```ts
static truncate(fn:  Fn(string:any), str: string, width: number, tail: string = ""): string,number
```

Truncate text to fit width.

**Parameters**

- `fn` (` Fn(string:any)`) — a function that can measure text width
- `str` (`string`) — text to truncate
- `width` (`number`) — width to fit
- `tail` (`string`; default `""`) — text to indicate overflow such as "...". Default is empty "".

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/UI.ts:50`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/UI.ts#L50)

**[Experimental]** An abstract class that represents an UI element. It wraps a [`Group`](#pt-group) and supports UI event handling.
Extend this class to create custom UI elements.

- `shape` (`string`) — specifies the shape of the Group

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/UI.ts:331`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/UI.ts#L331)

<a id="ui-uibutton-on-context-menu"></a>
##### `onContextMenu`

*source [`src/UI.ts:411`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/UI.ts#L411)*

```ts
onContextMenu(fn: UIHandler): number
```

Add a new contextmenu handler. `contextmenu` is similar to right click, see the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/contextmenu_event). Remember this button will also need to be tracked for events via `UI.track`. Also note that you may need to use `event.preventDefault()` in the callback function to prevent other events from triggering.

**Parameters**

- `fn` (`UIHandler`) — a [`UIHandler`](#types-uihandler) callback function: `fn( target:UI, pt:Pt, type:string, evt:MouseEvent )`

**Returns:** an id number that refers to this handler, for use in [`UIButton.offContextMenu`](#ui-uibutton-off-context-menu) or [`UI.off`](#ui-ui-off).


Add handlers for hover events. Remember this button will also need to be tracked for events via `UI.track`.

**Parameters**

- `enter` (`UIHandler`) — an optional [`UIHandler`](#types-uihandler) function to handle when pointer enters hover. Eg, `fn( target:UI, pt:Pt, type:string, evt:MouseEvent )`
- `leave` (`UIHandler`) — an optional [`UIHandler`](#types-uihandler) function to handle when pointer exits hover. Eg, `fn( target:UI, pt:Pt, type:string, evt:MouseEvent )`

**Returns:** id numbers that refer to enter/leave handlers, for use in [`UIButton.offHover`](#ui-uibutton-off-hover) or [`UI.off`](#ui-ui-off).

<a id="ui-uidragger"></a>
### `UIDragger`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/UI.ts:456`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/UI.ts#L456)

**Extends:** `UIButton`

[Experimental] A draggable UI that provides handler such as [`UIDragger.onDrag`](#ui-uidragger-on-drag) and [`UIDragger.onDrop`](#ui-uidragger-on-drop).

#### Constructors

<a id="ui-uidragger-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

*overrides `UIButton.__constructor` · source [`src/UI.ts:469`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/UI.ts#L469)*

```ts
new UIDragger(group: PtLikeIterable, shape: string, states:  = {}, id: string): UIDragger
```

Create a dragger which has all the states in UIButton, with additional "dragging" (a boolean indicating whether it's currently being dragged) and "offset" (a Pt representing the offset between this UI's position and the pointer's position when dragged) states. (See [`UI.state`](#ui-ui-state)) You may also create a new UIDragger using one of the static helper like [`UI.fromRectangle`](#ui-ui-static-from-rectangle) or [`UI.fromCircle`](#ui-ui-static-from-circle).

**Parameters**

- `group` (`PtLikeIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<PtLike> that defines the UI's appearance
- `shape` (`string`) — specifies the shape of the Group
- `states` (``; default `{}`) — Optional default state object
- `id` (`string`) — Optional id string


A convenient way to step through a range. Same as `for (i=0; i<range; i++)`, except this also stores the resulting return values at each step and return them as an array.

- `step` (`number`; default `1`)

**Returns:** an array of returned values at each step

```ts
static load(url: string, callback:  Fn(response:string, success:boolean)): void
```

A helper function to load data from a url via XMLHttpRequest GET. Since the response passed into callback is a string, if you're loading json data, you may use standard `JSON.parse(response)` to get a JSON object. For csv, try using a javascript csv library like papaparse or vega/datalib.

**Parameters**

- `callback` (` Fn(response:string, success:boolean)`) — a function to capture the data. It receives two parameters: a `response` as string, and a `success` status as boolean.

<a id="util-util-static-split"></a>

```ts
static split(pts: any[], size: number, stride: number, loopBack: boolean = false, matchSize: boolean = true): any[][]
```

Split an array into chunks of sub-array.

**Parameters**

- `pts` (`any[]`) — an array
- `size` (`number`) — chunk size, ie, number of items in a chunk
- `stride` (`number`) — optional parameter to "walk through" the array in steps
- `loopBack` (`boolean`; default `false`) — if `true`, always go through the array till the end and loop back to the beginning to complete the segments if needed.
- `matchSize` (`boolean`; default `true`) — if `true`, all chunks's length must match `size`.

<a id="util-util-static-stepper"></a>
##### `stepper`

*static · source [`src/Util.ts:289`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Util.ts#L289)*

```ts
static stepper(max: number, min: number = 0, stride: number = 1, callback:  Fn(n:number)):  ()
```

Create a convenient stepper. This returns a function which you can call repeatedly to step a counter.

**Parameters**

- `max` (`number`) — Maximum of the stepper range. The resulting stepper will return (min to max-1) values.
- `min` (`number`; default `0`) — Minimum of the stepper range. Default is 0.
- `stride` (`number`; default `1`) — Stride of the step. Default is 1.
- `callback` (` Fn(n:number)`) — An optional callback function `fn( step )`, which will be called each time when stepper function is called.

**Returns:** a function which will increment the stepper and return its value at each call.

**Example**

```ts
let counter = stepper(100); let c = counter(); c = counter(); ...
```

